Endpoint wiring is correct and consistent with the rest of `AgentHandler`: `services.dhcp` exists on `ServiceCollectionV3` (`src/maasservicelayer/services/__init__.py:279,658`), and the service raises exactly the `NotFoundException`/`ValidationException` mapped to the declared 404/422 (`src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py:126-138`). No consumer exists yet for `/dhcp-data` (grep finds only the new code and tests), so the wire contract is still free to change — worth getting right now.

Main concerns, in order:

1. Authorization granularity. The handler trusts any valid client certificate and returns the full DHCP inventory of an arbitrary `system_id` (host reservations with MAC addresses and hostnames, HA rack IPs, DNS/NTP servers). `RequireClientCertMiddleware` only proves "some enrolled agent" and stores the agent UUID in `request.scope["client_cn"]` (`src/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/client_certificate.py:45`), which this handler ignores. `/agents/{uuid}/config` has the same gap, so this follows existing practice — but the new endpoint broadens what one compromised agent can enumerate across the whole fleet. Either bind CN -> agent -> `rackcontroller_id` -> `system_id` and reject mismatches, or state the flat-trust model explicitly so it is a decision rather than an omission.

2. Layering. `AgentDHCPDataResponse` embeds the service-layer stdlib dataclasses (`VlanData`, `SubnetData`, ...) directly as the response schema, unlike every other response module in this tree (e.g. `CNAMERecordResponse` in `responses/domains.py`), so any service-layer field rename silently changes the agent-facing payload. Note pydantic v2 does not revalidate already-constructed dataclass instances (pydantic/pydantic#5621), so these annotations provide schema text only, no validation.

3. Caching. `/config` sets an `ETag` and declares `OPENAPI_ETAG_HEADER`; this endpoint, which agents will poll and whose payload is far larger (and duplicates every range under both `ipranges` and `subnets[].pools`), has neither.

4. Tests. Coverage of the 200 path is good; the 403 case re-tests global middleware already covered by `src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/test_client_certificate.py`, and several assertions only verify field copying, which AGENTS.md asks you to avoid.

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.201: The 200 entry declares no headers, unlike `/agents/{uuid}/config` which declares `OPENAPI_ETAG_HEADER` and sets `response.headers["ETag"]`. This payload is both the largest the agent fetches and the one it will poll; an ETag (e.g. hashing the serialized `DHCPDataForAgent`) would let agents skip unchanged configs. Also consider declaring 403 here, since `RequireClientCertMiddleware` can return it for this path.
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/handle.212: `system_id` is taken straight from the path with no check against the authenticated client. `RequireClientCertMiddleware` sets `request.scope["client_cn"]` (the agent UUID) and nothing here consumes it, so any enrolled agent can dump another rack's DHCP inventory — host reservations, MAC addresses, hostnames, HA rack IPs. Suggest resolving the agent from the CN and 403-ing when its `rackcontroller_id` does not map to `system_id`; if flat trust between agents is intentional, say so in the handler docstring.

src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.73: These are `maasservicelayer.models.dhcp` dataclasses used verbatim as the API schema, which couples the agent wire format to the service layer — a field rename in `SubnetData` silently becomes a breaking protocol change, and the three-tier split used elsewhere in this package (e.g. `CNAMERecordResponse` in `responses/domains.py`) is bypassed. Also note pydantic v2 does not revalidate already-built stdlib dataclass instances, so these annotations only document the schema; they do not enforce it. Recommend explicit response models (or at minimum a comment stating the coupling is deliberate because the agent is the sole consumer).
src/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/models.94: The f-string wrapper is a no-op: `href=self_base_hyperlink.rstrip("/")` is equivalent and matches `AgentConfigResponse.from_model` / `responses/domains.py:208`.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.368: This exercises `RequireClientCertMiddleware` (added by the fixture at `src/tests/maasapiserver/fixtures/app.py:102`), not the handler, and the 403-on-missing-CN behaviour is already asserted in `src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/middlewares/test_client_certificate.py`. Per AGENTS.md ("avoid trivial assertions", "keep tests minimal") this and `InjectTLSWithoutClientCert` can be dropped — unless the intent is to guard against `/dhcp-data` being added to the middleware's exemption list, in which case a comment saying so would help.
src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.386: The 404 and 422 tests differ only in the exception the mocked service raises and the expected status; both verify the shared exception middleware's mapping rather than handler logic. Collapsing them into one `@pytest.mark.parametrize("error,status", ...)` case would remove ~30 duplicated lines.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/internal/.69: `response.vlans == dhcp_data.vlans`, `response.interfaces == ...`, `response.ha_data == ...` assert plain field copying, and `kind` asserts a literal default — all tautological. The only behaviour worth pinning here is `hal_links.self.href` (the `rstrip("/")` handling); consider keeping that assertion and dropping the rest, since the handler test already covers the serialized payload.
